content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are the meat taken from the wing of a bird. They are popular worldwide for their juicy flavor and versatility, being suitable for frying, baking, grilling, and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a staple in barbecue and the American dish "Buffalo wings".
They contain more protein per ounce than most other chicken parts.
Wings can be prepared with or without skin, affecting taste and calorie count.
In the United States, over 1.5 billion servings of chicken wings are consumed each year.
The "NS" cooking method denotes preparation without added salt.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Wings supply phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immune health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as they deliver energy without added sugars.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Skin‑on wings contain a notable amount of saturated fat, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Prepared marinades can be high in salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings can be deep‑fried, baked, grilled, or braised in sauce. They are often marinated in spices, soy sauce, or yogurt‑based blends before cooking. Serve with dipping sauces, vegetable sides, or as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh wings should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen wings retain quality for up to 9 months at –18 °C. Thaw in the fridge rather than at room temperature before cooking.

coffee-cake-crumb-or-quick-bread-type.title: Coffee cake, crumb or quick‑bread type

content.title: About
content.content: Coffee cake is a soft, aromatic baked good that belongs to the crumb and quick‑bread category. It is leavened with baking powder rather than yeast and typically contains ground coffee, sugar, eggs, butter and flour. The flavor combines sweet notes with a subtle coffee bitterness, making it a popular snack for breakfast or a mid‑day treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In the United States and Canada the term “coffee cake” refers to this type of quick‑bread, while in Russia it is simply called “кофейный кекс”.
Traditional recipes often add a cinnamon‑nut crumble on top for extra crunch.
The batter can be prepared and baked in 30‑40 minutes without a long rise time.
Both instant coffee and freshly ground beans can be used, affecting the intensity of the coffee flavor.
Some regional versions are finished with a cream‑cheese glaze that adds a mild tang.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Coffee provides polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: A modest amount of caffeine can increase alertness and concentration.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and nuts add fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain flour supply B1, B2 and B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Nuts and dairy contribute magnesium, calcium and iron.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People who are sensitive to caffeine should limit their intake of coffee cake.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet versions can contribute to weight gain if eaten in excess.

items.title: Allergy to nuts or dairy
items.content: Many recipes include nuts and milk, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional coffee cake contains wheat flour and is not suitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve coffee cake sliced, often alongside a cup of coffee or tea. It can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature and can also be used as a base for dessert parfaits.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate for up to 1 week or freeze in sealed bags for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (a member of the cod family) is a lean white‑fleshed fish that is commonly baked or broiled. It has a mild flavor, low fat content, and a high protein level, making it a popular choice for healthy meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting is found in the cold waters of the North Atlantic and the Baltic Sea.
In the United States, whiting is often sold as fillets and used in fish‑and‑chips style dishes.
The fish can grow up to 30 cm in length and weigh around 300 g.
A 100 g serving provides roughly 85 kcal, making it a low‑calorie protein source.
Whiting is traditionally used in European coastal cuisines, especially in fried preparations.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g portion supplies about 18 g of complete protein, essential for muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Whiting contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and iodine
items.content: Whiting is a good source of selenium, an antioxidant, and iodine, important for thyroid health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, whiting still contributes omega‑3s that help cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: As a marine species, whiting can contain trace amounts of mercury and other heavy metals; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive baking or broiling can degrade heat‑sensitive vitamins such as B12.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Season whiting fillets with herbs, lemon, and a drizzle of olive oil, then bake or broil until opaque and flaky. Serve with steamed vegetables, roasted potatoes, or whole‑grain salads. The mild flesh also works well in fish tacos, soups, or as a protein addition to grain bowls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh whiting refrigerated at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic or placed in an airtight container, and use within 2 days. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Discard any fish with a strong, ammonia‑like odor, as it indicates spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: The white Roll bun is a soft, slightly sweet hamburger bun made from wheat flour, water, yeast, sugar, salt and a small amount of butter. It has a smooth golden crust and a light, airy interior, making it perfect for holding juicy fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Roll bun is typically 10 cm in diameter, matching the standard hamburger size.
The traditional recipe includes milk, which gives the dough a softer texture and richer flavor.
In some countries these buns are simply called “white hamburger buns” and are a staple in fast‑food menus.
Buns are often lightly toasted before serving to add a crisp outer layer.
Variants with sesame or poppy seeds are common for added taste and visual appeal.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The bun provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, which support metabolism.

items.title: Modest protein content
items.content: Each bun delivers about 4 g of protein, contributing to muscle maintenance.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture makes it gentle on the stomach, suitable for children and seniors.

items.title: Fiber (in whole‑grain versions)
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, the bun adds dietary fiber that promotes gut health.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Contains gluten, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapidly absorbed carbs can raise blood sugar, which diabetics should monitor.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add extra salt; those watching sodium intake should consider this.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Allergy to wheat may cause reactions when consuming the bun.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the Roll bun as the base for hamburgers, sandwiches, or hot sliders. Slice it open, lightly toast on a grill or toaster, then add a patty, cheese, vegetables and sauces. It also works well for appetizers such as smoked salmon with cream cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buns in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 3 months). Thaw at room temperature before use and optionally toast.
